A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a clear discrimination of WW and gg production of the Higgs boson is possible only in the case of a very high luminosity of the LHC.
the Higgs signal in WW→H is more easily seen than in the gluon-gluon fusion process.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Higgs boson is produced in association with two jets, and these jets are produced in the forward direction, i.e. with large rapidities.
a rapidity gap technique is not a panacea for the discrimination problem.
